evidence.claim: The hydration reactor works at 199 C and 3480 kPa with about 10 mol water per mol EO; its outlet is 88.03 % water, 1.55 % EO, 10.24 % MEG, 0.10 % DEG, 0.08 % TEG (mol). HYSYS models it as a conversion reactor; the text calls it a plug flow reactor of 77.8 m x 0.55 m with 3 min residence.
limits: Aspen HYSYS 11 simulation, not measured.
Table 1's 85/15 selectivity and Table 3's outlet (about 98 % MEG among the glycols formed, derived) disagree; the reactor's sense of heat (endothermic in the text) is not checked.

evidence.claim: Water is removed in three evaporators at 1600, 804.5 and 400 kPa (Q1 + Q2 + Q3 = 17.76 MW) and a vacuum dehydration column (15 trays, 15/20 kPa; 107.4 MW condenser, 94.1 MW reboiler). From Table 3 the evaporators take about 30 % of the water of stream 4, not the 75 % of the text.
limits: Aspen HYSYS 11 simulation, not measured.
The 29.8 % is Lab's derivation (cases/ethylene-glycol-shehata-2024/STREAM_AUDIT.md); the text says about 75 %.
The text's 85 mm Hg (11.3 kPa) differs from Table 1's 15/20 kPa.

evidence.claim: MEG is separated from DEG and TEG in a 26-tray column at 12.5/13 kPa to keep below 170 C; MEG 0.9977 mol fraction at 1113 kmol/h, DEG+TEG 20.43 kmol/h at 190 C in Fig. 5. The text says MEG is a side stream; Fig. 5 shows MEG leaving at the condenser pressure.
limits: Aspen HYSYS 11 simulation, not measured.
The DEG+TEG bottoms at 190 C in Fig. 5 is above the 170 C the text gives for MEG.

evidence.claim: All evaporator vapours and the dehydration distillate are mixed (WATER REC, 9867 kmol/h, 98.12 % water, 1.73 % EO), chilled to 0.77 C at 10 kPa, pumped to 3500 kPa and returned (stream 11, 9870 kmol/h) with 1130 kmol/h of fresh water; the recycle is about 8.5 times the fresh EO (1160 kmol/h).
limits: Aspen HYSYS 11 simulation, not measured.
Stream 11 and WATER REC differ by 3 kmol/h of water, outside rounding: HYSYS's recycle tolerance, which carries into the plant balance.

plain.title: Ethylene oxide hydration: liquid reactor at 199 C and 3480 kPa with about 10 mol water per mol oxide
plain.when: Ethylene oxide reacts with water to MEG, and with MEG and DEG to the heavier glycols.
plain.do: Run the reactor in the liquid at 199 C and 3480 kPa with about 10 mol of water per mol oxide (Shehata et al. 2024, p. 8).
plain.why: The water excess makes the oxide meet water rather than glycol.
plain.check: Outlet 88.03 / 1.55 / 10.24 / 0.10 / 0.08 mol % water / EO / MEG / DEG / TEG (Table 3, stream 4).
plain.note: Numbers: Shehata et al. 2024, p. 8 (199 C, 3480 kPa, water to EO 10:1) and Table 3, stream 4 (p. 10).

decisions.obstacle: Consecutive reactions to DEG and TEG lower the MEG yield.
decisions.operation: Conversion reactor in HYSYS (Table 1); plug flow reactor 77.8 m x 0.55 m, 3 min, in the text (p. 8).
decisions.expected_change: About 98 % of the glycols formed are MEG (derived from Table 3).
limits: Table 1 gives 85/15 MEG/(DEG+TEG), Table 3 about 98/2; the text calls the reaction endothermic.
Draft, written by an AI session from the case files (2026-11-27); not reviewed.

plain.title: Water from a dilute glycol solution: three evaporators at falling pressure, then a vacuum column
plain.when: The reactor effluent holds 88.03 mol % water and 10.24 mol % MEG.
plain.do: Flash it in three evaporators at 1600, 804.5 and 400 kPa, then finish in a 15-tray column at 15/20 kPa (Shehata et al. 2024, Fig. 5, Table 1).
plain.why: The evaporators take part of the water at higher pressure; the column under vacuum keeps the glycol bottoms cool.
plain.check: MEG column feed carries no water in Table 3; the column duties are 107.4 / 94.1 MW (Table 8).
plain.note: Numbers: Fig. 5 (1600, 804.5, 400 kPa; stream 5 is the first evaporator's liquid), Table 1 (15 trays, 15/20 kPa), Table 3 (stream 4: 88.03 % water, 10.24 % MEG), Table 8 (DEH CON Q 107392.75 kW, DEH REQ Q 94108.24 kW, i.e. 107.4 / 94.1 MW).

decisions.obstacle: Much water to remove from a heat-sensitive glycol.
decisions.mechanism: Evaporation in stages, then vacuum distillation.
decisions.operation: EVA_1-3 with duties Q1-Q3 (17.76 MW together) and a dehydration tower.
decisions.expected_change: Water-free glycol to the MEG column.
alternatives: Ethylene carbonate route with near-stoichiometric water (same paper)
limits: The evaporators take about 30 % of the water by Table 3, not 75 % as the text says.
The HYSYS model gives each evaporator its own heat input; the text says the vapour of each heats the next.
